title: Auto-fixing cloud misconfigurations
summary: Most cloud breaches start with a setting left open. An agent finds them and fixes them the safe way: in code.

steps.label: finding
steps.title: The scanner flags a risky setting
steps.text: Security posture tools check every cloud resource against best-practice rules, continuously.
payload: Anyone with the link can download the files.

steps.label: inspect
steps.title: Check context before acting
steps.text: Not every public bucket is a mistake; website assets are meant to be public. The agent checks tags, contents and recent access first.
payload: Looks like customer data, not website files.

steps.label: pull request
steps.title: Fix it in code, not by clicking
steps.text: If you fix the live setting only, the next deploy puts the old one back. The agent changes the infrastructure-as-code file so the fix sticks.

steps.label: please approve
steps.title: Ask the right person
steps.text: The owner tag tells the agent exactly who to ask, so it doesn't go to a busy central security queue.
payload: "customer-exports is public and holds order data. Approve the PR to close it?"

steps.label: deploy
steps.title: Merged, deployed, verified
steps.text: After deployment the scanner checks again to confirm the finding is really gone.
